values.spoken: October thirtieth, twenty twenty-four

values.display: associate a security group with multiple VPCs in the same Region
values.spoken: one security group, several VPCs in the same Region

evidence.quote: If you have workloads running in multiple VPCs that share network security requirements, you can use the Security Group VPC Associations feature to associate a security group with multiple VPCs in the same Region. This enables you to manage and maintain security groups in one place for multiple VPCs in your account.

| [Security Group VPC Associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-assoc.html) | This feature enables you to associate a security group with multiple VPCs in the same Region. | October 30, 2024 |

values.display: cannot associate a default security group with another VPC or associate a security group with a default VPC
values.spoken: default security groups and default VPCs are excluded

evidence.quote: The VPC and security group must be in the same AWS Region.
You cannot associate a default security group with another VPC or associate a security group with a default VPC.

claim: VPC Block Public Access (BPA), added November 19, 2024, blocks resources in the VPCs and subnets you own in a Region from reaching or being reached from the internet through internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways; it is one account-level setting per Region, with exclusions.
question: What is VPC Block Public Access and when did it arrive?

values.display: November 19, 2024
values.spoken: November nineteenth, twenty twenty-four

values.display: block resources in VPCs and subnets that you own in a Region from reaching or being reached from the internet through internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways
values.spoken: one switch that blocks internet gateway traffic for a whole account in a Region

evidence.quote: | [VPC Block Public Access (BPA)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-vpc-bpa.html) | VPC Block public Access (BPA) enables you to block resources in VPCs and subnets that you own in a Region from reaching or being reached from the internet through internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways. | November 19, 2024 |

VPC Block Public Access (BPA) is a centralized security feature that authoritatively prevents public internet access to VPC resources across an entire AWS account. It ensures compliance with security requirements while providing flexibility for specific exceptions and audit capabilities.

note: FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed. Older 'block all internet access' answers rely on security groups, network ACLs and SCPs; BPA is the current best answer for an account-wide block.

claim: VPC BPA has two modes: bidirectional blocks all traffic to and from internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways in the Region (except excluded VPCs and subnets); ingress-only blocks internet traffic into the VPCs but still allows traffic through NAT gateways and egress-only internet gateways, because those only allow outbound connections.
question: What is the difference between VPC BPA bidirectional mode and ingress-only mode?

values.display: blocks all traffic to and from internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways
values.spoken: bidirectional: nothing in or out through the internet gateway

values.display: Only traffic to and from NAT gateways and egress-only internet gateways is allowed
values.spoken: ingress-only: outbound through NAT or egress-only gateway still works

evidence.quote: VPC BPA bidirectional mode blocks all traffic to and from internet gateways and egress-only internet gateways in this Region (except for excluded VPCs and subnets).

VPC BPA ingress-only mode blocks all internet traffic to the VPCs in this Region (except for VPCs or subnets which are excluded). Only traffic to and from NAT gateways and egress-only internet gateways is allowed because these gateways only allow outbound connections to be established.

claim: You can create a maximum of 50 VPC BPA exclusions per account per Region (adjustable); an exclusion for a VPC applies to all subnets in that VPC, and exclusions can be created before BPA is turned on.
question: How many VPC BPA exclusions can an account create?

values.display: maximum of 50 exclusions
values.spoken: fifty exclusions per account per Region

evidence.quote: You can create a maximum of 50 exclusions.

You can create VPC BPA exclusions for VPCs and subnets even when VPC BPA is not enabled on the account to ensure that there is no traffic disruption to the exclusions when VPC BPA is turned on. An exclusion for a VPC automatically applies to all subnets in the VPC.

| VPC Block Public Access exclusions per account per Region | 50 | Yes. To request an increase, see [Request a service quota increase](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/create-service-quota-increase.html) in the AWS Support User Guide. | The number of [VPC BPA exclusions](security-vpc-bpa-basics.md#security-vpc-bpa-exclusions) you can create in an account. |

claim: VPC BPA blocks all inbound and outbound traffic of NAT gateways and internet-facing Network and Application Load Balancers, because they need an internet gateway for internet connectivity; private connectivity such as Site-to-Site VPN, transit gateway, Client VPN and Verified Access is not affected.
question: Which resources does VPC BPA block, and which private connectivity does it leave alone?

values.display: NAT gateways require an internet gateway for internet connectivity
values.spoken: NAT gateways are blocked too, because they sit behind the internet gateway

values.display: is not blocked or impacted by VPC BPA
values.spoken: VPN, transit gateway and Direct Connect private paths are untouched

evidence.quote: **NAT gateway**: All inbound and outbound traffic is blocked. NAT gateways require an internet gateway for internet connectivity.
**Internet-facing Application Load Balancer**: All inbound and outbound traffic is blocked. Internet-facing Application Load Balancers require an internet gateway for internet connectivity.
Traffic related to private connectivity, such as traffic for the following services and resources, is not blocked or impacted by VPC BPA:

note: The private-connectivity list on the page: AWS Client VPN, AWS CloudWAN, AWS Outposts local gateway, AWS Site-to-Site VPN, Transit gateway, AWS Verified Access. Direct Connect public virtual interfaces are blocked.

claim: Since December 1, 2024 an AWS Organizations declarative policy can enforce VPC BPA on every account in the organization; the policy can decide whether exclusions are allowed, but exclusions themselves must still be created in the account that owns the VPC.
question: Can VPC Block Public Access be enforced across an organization, and what can the policy not do?

values.display: December 1, 2024
values.spoken: December first, twenty twenty-four

values.display: cannot create exclusions with the policy
values.spoken: the policy cannot create exclusions

evidence.quote: | [Declarative policy support for VPC BPA](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-vpc-bpa.html#security-vpc-bpa-exclusions-orgs) | If you are using AWS Organizations to manage accounts in your organization, you can use a declarative policy to enforce VPC BPA on the accounts in the organization. | December 1, 2024 |

You can use the VPC BPA declarative policy to configure if exclusions are allowed, but you cannot create exclusions with the policy. To create exclusions, you still have to create them in the account that owns the VPC.

claim: Since August 8, 2024 VPCs and subnets support private IPv6 addresses, which are not and cannot be advertised on the internet from AWS, are available only through Amazon VPC IPAM, and have no charge.
question: What are private IPv6 addresses in a VPC, and since when do they exist?

values.display: August 8, 2024
values.spoken: August eighth, twenty twenty-four

values.display: not advertised and cannot be advertised on the Internet from AWS
values.spoken: private IPv6: never advertised to the internet

values.display: no charge for private IPv6 addresses
values.spoken: private IPv6 addresses are free

evidence.quote: | [Private IPv6 addressing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-ip-addressing.html#vpc-ipv6-addresses-private) | Information about private IPv6 addressing was added. Private IPv6 addresses are only available in Amazon VPC IP Address Manager. | August 8, 2024 |
Private IPv6 addresses are IPv6 addresses that are not advertised and cannot be advertised on the Internet from AWS.
There is no charge for private IPv6 addresses.

note: Older material says all VPC IPv6 addresses are public and globally unique; that is still true for Amazon-provided public IPv6 (see vpc-ipv6-amazon-provided-public).

claim: Amazon-provided IPv6 addresses are always advertised on the internet and are globally unique, so they are reachable over the internet; you control reachability with subnet routing, security groups and network ACLs.
question: Are Amazon-provided IPv6 addresses public?

values.display: always advertised on the internet
values.spoken: public IPv6 is always advertised; routing and security groups decide reachability

evidence.quote: Amazon-provided IPv6 addresses are always advertised on the internet. They are globally unique, and therefore reachable over the internet. You can control whether resources such as EC2 instances are reachable using their IPv6 addresses by controlling routing for your subnets, or by using security groups and network ACLs.

claim: A VPC can have up to 5 IPv6 CIDR blocks sized from /44 to /60 in increments of /4, and an IPv6 subnet can be sized from /44 to /64 in increments of /4; a single IPv6 CIDR block can be added when the VPC is created.
question: What IPv6 CIDR sizes can a VPC and a subnet have?

values.display: from /44 to /60 in increments of /4
values.spoken: VPC: slash forty-four to slash sixty

values.display: between /44 and /64 in increments of /4
values.spoken: subnet: slash forty-four to slash sixty-four

values.display: up to five IPv6 CIDR blocks
values.spoken: up to five IPv6 blocks per VPC

evidence.quote: You can associate a single IPv6 CIDR block when you create a new VPC or you can associate up to five IPv6 CIDR blocks from `/44` to `/60` in increments of `/4`.
Possible IPv6 netmask lengths are between `/44` and `/64` in increments of `/4`.

note: Tiered IPv6 sizes arrived November 16, 2023 (What's New, blocked by robots.txt; date from the change feed). Older material knows only a /56 VPC block and /64 subnets; the current pages do not state that old value verbatim, so no changed.was.
